purpose: Sertaconazole nitrate is used to treat a common fungal skin infection called athlete's foot (tinea pedis). It helps clear up the itching, burning, cracking, and scaling that comes with this infection. It is applied directly to the skin and works right where the infection is.
how_it_works: This medication works by attacking the outer layer of the fungus and breaking it down. It pokes holes in the fungal cell wall, causing the fungus to leak and die. By killing the fungus, your skin can heal and your symptoms go away.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice mild skin reactions where they apply the cream, such as redness, burning, stinging, itching, or tenderness. These reactions are usually mild and temporary. Contact your doctor if they are severe or do not go away.
warnings: This medication is for use on the skin only — do not use it in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medicine. If your infection does not improve after 4 weeks of treatment, contact your doctor. Stop using it and call your doctor right away if you have severe skin irritation or an allergic reaction like rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing.
typical_dosing: Apply the cream to the affected skin and a small area around it two times a day (morning and evening) for 4 weeks. Make sure the area is clean and dry before applying. Wash your hands before and after using the cream.
